newsitem.title: USA: Rubin repeats US position on strong dollar.
newsitem.headline: Rubin repeats US position on strong dollar.

text.p: U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin repeated on Tuesday that the United States favored a strong dollar, adding "it's been strong for some time now."
The statement was a reiteration of the recent U.S. position on the currency, suggesting that the United States did not favor seeing the dollar appreciate from around present levels.
Rubin, speaking with reporters following testimony on the administration budget before the House Ways and Means Committee, also said that a strong Japanese economy was in everybody's interest.
"It's very important for the whole world that Japan have a strong economy," Rubin told reporters, adding, "One cannot help but feel cautious concern about the prospects for the Japanese economy."
"It is very important that Japan for its own sake and the rest of the world have a macroeconomic policy that is designed to provide strong investment-led demand," he added.
